title: Gemini 3.1 Pro on iac-bench 2026-10
summary: How Gemini 3.1 Pro did on iac-bench 2026-10: an overall composite of 73.0, scores per fixture, strengths, weaknesses and the patterns in its OpenTofu modules.
body_markdown:
Developer Google


API identifier` gemini-3.1-pro-preview`


Access Gemini API


Weights Closed


List price (USD / M tokens, in / out) 2.00 / 12.00 (OpenRouter, 2026-10-23)


Evaluated 2026-10-22 (generation) · 2026-10-23 (judge)


Attempts 9 (3 fixtures × 3 samples)


**Overall composite** **73.0** (95% CI 69.2–76.2)


Rank 7 of 10 (95% rank interval 6–9)


Mechanical only / judge only 71.9 (rank 7) / 71.9 (rank 8)


Failed gates · insecure attempts 0/9 · 5/9


Estimated cost, all 9 attempts $2.26


## Summary


Gemini 3.1 Pro writes the leanest modules among the full-size models: few inputs, short files, low token use. All 9 of its modules planned. Five of the 9 had security findings, all from settings left unset rather than settings exposed as inputs:


- App Service (3/3):` https_only` and the basic-auth publishing flags are never set, so the provider defaults leave HTTP and shared-credential publishing open.
- Cloud SQL (2/3):` ssl_mode` is never set, so unencrypted connections are accepted.


It is also the only model with no` validation` block in any of its nine modules.

Definitions are in[Scoring criteria](https://www.massdriver.cloud/blogs/iac-bench-2026-10-scoring-criteria) .


## Strengths


- **Hardcoded S3 baseline (3/3).** All four public-access-block settings, unconditional encryption, and bucket-owner-enforced ownership.
- **No knobs for network exposure or IAM on Cloud SQL.**` ipv4_enabled = false` is a literal, and the IAM authentication flag is merged after consumer flags so it cannot be overridden.
- **No credentials taken as input.** IAM users only on Cloud SQL, with the service-account suffix stripped correctly.
- **Restraint.** No restraint item lost on any fixture, and the smallest App Service interface in the field (median 11 inputs).
- **Low cost and token use.** About 4.7–7.7k output tokens per attempt.


## Weaknesses


- **App Service` H1` and` H2` (security findings, 3/3).** HTTPS-only and the basic-auth publishing flags are absent on the web app and the slot (excerpt below).
- **Cloud SQL` H2` (security finding, 2/3).**` ip_configuration` omits` ssl_mode` . The third attempt hardcodes it correctly.
- **No input validation (9/9).** *Variables and validation* scored 0 in every attempt. The judge named realistic breakages, such as zone balancing turned on by default for a plan size that doesn't support it.
- **Domain gaps:**


- no Cloud SQL login-role grant (E6), connection logging (E8) or Query Insights (E9), all 0/3;
- no tags input on App Service (` H8` , 0/3);
- no S3 access logging (` H9` ,` H13` ).


## Characteristic patterns


- **Pass-through inputs.** Variables map one to one onto resource attributes (` sku_name` ,` disk_type` ,` availability_type` ). *Interface design* scored 1 in 7/9.
- **Almost no locals.** App Service slot and app blocks are duplicated verbatim.
- **Minimal documentation.** No README in any attempt. Every variable has a description, but one description is inverted ("whether or not to allow Terraform to destroy the instance" on a deletion-protection input).
- **It under-builds rather than over-builds.** Missing items dominate its losses.


## Representative excerpt


` G003/gemini-3.1-pro-preview-e1/main.tf` lines 45–58


```text
resource "azurerm_linux_web_app" "this" {
name                = var.app_name
location            = azurerm_resource_group.this.location
resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.this.name
service_plan_id     = azurerm_service_plan.this.id


identity {
type = "SystemAssigned"
}


site_config {
application_stack {
docker_image_name   = var.container_image
docker_registry_url = var.container_registry_url


```


An otherwise complete resource that never sets` https_only` or the basic-auth publishing flags. The same omission appears on all six App Service web apps and slots this model wrote.


## Notes on the judge


Insecure configuration is scored by the rubric, not the judge, so the security findings move this model's judge grade very little. On Cloud SQL, the attempt with a security finding received the highest judge grade of the three, and the secure attempt the lowest. The composite takes both into account. Read either component alone and you get a misleading picture.
